title: P7 topology-local content-addressed checkpoint control
hypothesis: Replacing replicated transaction checkpoint payloads with topology-local immutable content-addressed blobs can strictly reduce persisted regular-file payload bytes in both full-process and pooled-expert controls without changing exact trajectory state, transaction identity, worker-result reuse, or fresh-coordinator recovery.

use_case.claim: Decide whether content-addressed checkpoint storage closes the repeated-state problem observed in the persisted sparse trajectory, without making a model-quality or timing claim.

baseline.label: Replicated transaction checkpoint layout
baseline.description: Every transaction retains its own pre-state and applied model and optimizer safetensors payloads under the existing exact persisted trajectory.

primary_metric.label: Minimum topology persisted-byte reduction
primary_metric.description: The smaller of the full-process and pooled-expert persisted-byte reduction fractions. The gate tests positive direction only; strict reduction in both topologies is a separate guardrail, and no post-measurement materiality threshold is introduced.

repeated_validation_suite.label: Two independent opposite-order one-thread comparisons
repeated_validation_suite.description: The primary runs replicated then content-addressed storage. The repeat reverses the order. Storage, semantic state, identities, and recovery results must reproduce; timings and process-memory observations remain environmental.

final_holdout_suite.label: Storage, exactness, and recovery comparison
final_holdout_suite.description: For three sequential steps and both process topologies, compare physical regular-file payload totals, semantic trajectory evidence, final model and optimizer identities, transaction identities, worker loss, fresh-process recovery, and duplicate-apply rejection.

guardrails.label: Strict reduction in both topologies
guardrails.description: Content-addressed regular-file payload bytes must be lower than replicated bytes for both the full-process and pooled-expert roots.

guardrails.label: Opposite-order storage repeat
guardrails.description: The repeat must reproduce every storage total, blob count, checkpoint-reference count, and reused-reference count exactly.

guardrails.label: Semantic and transaction identity
guardrails.description: Every non-environmental trajectory field and every transaction identity must match between replicated and content-addressed layouts and across the two runs.

guardrails.label: Durable recovery and at-most-once apply
guardrails.description: Accepted worker results must survive loss without recomputation, and a fresh coordinator must recover the published checkpoint while rejecting duplicate apply.

guardrails.label: Closed content-addressed storage
guardrails.description: Canonical references, exact blob membership, safetensors digests and lengths, closed directories, and physical byte accounting must validate without unlisted material.

guardrails.label: Bounded host load
guardrails.description: At most one child process may execute at a time and all numerical libraries must remain on one compute thread.

independent_variables.label: Replicated or topology-local content-addressed checkpoints
independent_variables.description: The baseline writes checkpoint payloads into each transaction. The candidate writes each immutable model or optimizer payload once per topology and stores canonical references in transactions.

independent_variables.label: Primary and reversed execution order
independent_variables.description: One run executes the replicated layout first and one executes the content-addressed layout first so a fixed order cannot silently determine the timing comparison.

controlled_variables.label: Frozen T1 data, model, routing, and optimizer trajectory
controlled_variables.description: Both layouts use the same frozen dataset revision, campaign dimensions, initialization, three cursors, four experts, routing, clipping, frozen head, and coordinator-owned AdamW updates.

controlled_variables.label: Independent full-process and pooled-expert roots
controlled_variables.description: Full-process and pooled-expert blob stores remain topology-local and do not share files, so their storage totals remain independent controls.

controlled_variables.label: Matched worker and coordinator failure boundaries
controlled_variables.description: Both layouts lose a worker after an accepted result is durable and lose coordinator progress after an applied checkpoint is published but before the manifest phase is committed.

controlled_variables.label: Bounded one-thread local runtime
controlled_variables.description: Both runs use one numerical compute thread, at most one child process, a 120-second operation timeout, and a 0.01-second external RSS sampling interval.
